newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CBO urged to show impact of tax changes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CBO urged to show impact of tax changes.

text.p: Republican leaders urged the Congressional Budget Office in its next estimate of the federal deficit to take into account the positive impact on the economy from cutting the capital gains tax rate, according to a letter released Monday.
CBO, the official budget analysis arm of Congress, has in the past resisted use of what is termed "dynamic scoring" of economic effects on the budget of changes in tax policy.
House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott requested this type of analysis be used in the CBO's mid-year re-estimate of the budget deficit.

"We believe it woudl be exceedingly useful for CBO to estimate the positive economic effects that will result from cutting the capital gains rate in haalf, and indexing gains for inflation," Lott of Mississippi and Gingrich of Georgia wrote. House Majority Leader Dick Armey, Republican of Texas, also signed the letter.

CBO, a non-partisan analysis group which is not bound to follow the direction of either political party, calculated last month it had underestimated the health of the economy and revised its forecast for the budget deficit to include additional revenues of $225 billion over five years.
It also calculates the positive impact on the deficit which will stem from balancing the budget. This impact, called the "fiscal dividend" is estimated to total $77 billion over five years.
Based on these measures of feedback on the budget, the Republican leaders recommended the agency look at capital gains tax rate cuts and indexing in the same positive light.

They also asked CBO to conduct an analysis of the effects of tax policy changes and tax cuts. Typically, the Joint Committee on Taxation forecasts revenue effects of tax policy changes but does not evaluate the economic impact of taxation.
